requirement_text.REQ-067: Port src/api/pagination.zig (406 lines, R-Co's API-06) as Letflow.Api.Pagination -- the shared cursor encode/decode, prefix validation, expiry checking, page-size validation, and standardised page response that every S4 list endpoint delegates to. Port the constants exactly: MAX_PAGE_SIZE 200, DEFAULT_PAGE_SIZE 50, MIN_PAGE_SIZE 1, CURSOR_EXPIRY_US 86_400_000_000. A requested page size above MAX_PAGE_SIZE, below MIN_PAGE_SIZE, or non-numeric is a 400, not a silent clamp. A cursor carries a type prefix so a cursor minted by one endpoint cannot be replayed against another. An expired cursor is rejected. SECURITY (INV-1, INV-5): the decoded cursor struct must have no tenant/schema field -- tenant scoping comes exclusively from REQ-072's future resolved request context, never from the cursor.

This is non-blocking and about the design's prose citation, not the implementation -- you do not need to fix the design doc, just implement the error shape as specified (both atoms still map to a 400 via `Letflow.Api.Error`).

result.summary: Implemented lib/letflow/api/pagination.ex per lib/letflow/design/api-pagination.md in full: constants (@max_page_size 200, @default_page_size 50, @min_page_size 1, @cursor_expiry_us 86_400_000_000) with public accessors; Cursor struct (inner-only field, structural INV-1/INV-5 enforcement); Page envelope struct with Jason.Encoder derive; parse_page_size_param/1 and validate_page_size/1 as a split pair per design §0.1 (reject-not-clamp, single :page_size_too_large atom for both 0 and >200 per design §0.2); page_response/2; encode_cursor/1; decode_cursor/4 (default expiry_window_us \\ @cursor_expiry_us) performing base64url decode -> prefix match -> expiry check in that order with the design's flagged distinct :invalid_cursor atom for malformed-timestamp-slice cases; build_raw_cursor/3 and build_raw_cursor_timestamp_key/4; parse_int_from_cursor/3 and find_nth_colon/2. No SQL/Ecto/Repo call anywhere in the module -- confirmed by inspection, this module is pure per design §9. Every public function has a @doc. mix compile --warnings-as-errors and mix format --check-formatted both pass. One implementation deviation from a literal transliteration, not from the design's specified shape: decode_cursor/4's timestamp-slice extraction uses binary_part/3 instead of a <<_::binary-size(offset), ts::binary-size(len)>> match, because the match triggered 'variable accessed inside size() but defined outside the match, use the pin operator' warnings under --warnings-as-errors (offset/len are runtime-computed, not literals) -- binary_part/3 is semantically identical and still ports the same slice-then-parse behavior the design specifies in prose. No file outside lib/letflow/api/pagination.ex was modified by this work (handoffs/orchestrator.log and handoffs/registry.json show as modified in git status but were changed by another process/session, not by this agent, and are left untouched).
